'''Sahati Suharto''' (10 March 1932{{spnd}}14 April 2020) was an Indonesian chemist and academic administrator from the [[University of Indonesia]] who became the dean of the university's Faculty of Math and Natural Sciences from 1984 to 1988.

== Career ==
[[File:Sahati_Suharto,_Laporan_Rektor_Tahun_1984_(1985),_p269.jpg|left|thumb|Sahati in her academic robe.]]
Born on 10 March 1932 in Jakarta,<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=15 April 2020 |title=Berita Duka : Dra. Sahati Suharto Dekan ke-6 FMIPA UI Wafat |url=https://www.sci.ui.ac.id/berita-duka-dra-sahati-suharto-dekan-ke-6-fmipa-ui-wafat/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812094824/https://www.sci.ui.ac.id/berita-duka-dra-sahati-suharto-dekan-ke-6-fmipa-ui-wafat/ |archive-date=12 August 2020 |access-date=21 February 2025 |work=FMIPA UI}}</ref> Sahati received her bachelor's degree in chemistry from the [[Bandung Institute of Technology]] in 1963.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Society |first=American Chemical |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ArIkAQAAIAAJ |title=Chemical Research Faculties: An International Directory, 1988 |date=1988 |publisher=American Chemical Society |isbn=978-0-8412-1017-2 |pages=137 |language=en}}</ref> Sahati taught [[inorganic chemistry]] at the university and translated several textbooks on the subject. She was appointed as the chair of the chemistry department from 1975 until 1976. Around November 1976, Sahati conducted a two-week trip to Japan, where she visited universities and chemical facilities.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5lVDAQAAIAAJ |title=国際交流 |date=1976 |publisher=国際交流基金 |pages=61 |language=ja}}</ref> Two years later, she was appointed by dean of the Faculty of Exact Sciences and Natural Sciences [[Soekarja Somadikarta]] to serve as his deputy for academic, research, and community service.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Department of Education and Culture, University of Indonesia |url=https://lib.ui.ac.id/detail?id=76125&lokasi=lokal |title=Laporan Rektor Tahun 1984 |publisher=Panitia Dies Natalis XXXVI Universitas Indonesia |year=1985 |pages=269–271}}</ref> She served in this position until 19 November 1984.<ref name=":0" />
[[File:Handover_of_FMIPA_UI_dean_from_Soekarja_Somadikarta_to_Sahati_Suharto,_Laporan_Rektor_Tahun_1984_(1985),_p271.jpg|thumb|Sahati's inauguration as dean of the faculty of math and natural sciences.]]
On 19 November 1984, Sahati became the dean of University of Indonesia's Faculty of Math and Natural Science.<ref name=":1" /> She was the second woman to hold this position.<ref name=":0" /> During her tenure, she was sued by one of her students, whom she expelled due to bad grades. Sahati had previously offered him a chance to re-apply but was refused.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Basri dan |first1=Agus |last2=Indrayati |first2=Sri |date=2 April 1988 |title=Tidak Lulus Rektor Digugat |url=https://www.tempo.co/politik/tidak-lulus-rektor-digugat-1057900 |url-access=subscription |access-date=21 February 2025 |work=Tempo}}</ref> She served in the position until she was replaced by [[Parangtopo Sutokusumo]] on 1 March 1988.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sutokusumo |first=Parangtopo |url=https://lib.ui.ac.id/detail.jsp?id=77461#digital#digital |title=Faktor Penentu Pengembangan IPTEK di Negara Berkembang |date=1988 |publisher=UI Press |pages=23}}</ref> Sahati continued teaching chemistry at the university until her retirement and supported efforts to introduce chemistry to high school students, urging students not to fear chemistry.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 July 1988 |title=Pendapat Dosen Kimia: Cukup Dikenalkan Saja |access-date= |work=Kompas |pages=6}}</ref>

Sahati died on 14 April 2020 at her residence in Bandung, West Java.<ref name=":0" />
